after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 6 & -2 \\ 3 & -1 \\ -6 & 2\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ and vector $b$ shown above. If the general least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R,
$$

what is the value of $-10a+\frac{6b}{c}?$
after.worked_solution:
The least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

$$
{A}^{T}\,Ax={A}^{T}b
$$

Notice that the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent. So first, let's write down the normal equation in matrix form:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}3 & 6 & 3 & -6 \\ -1 & -2 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 6 & -2 \\ 3 & -1 \\ -6 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 6 & 3 & -6 \\ -1 & -2 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}90 & -30 \\ -30 & 10\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-27 \\ 9\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the above matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}90 & -30 & -27 \\ -30 & 10 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}90 & -30 & -27 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we have  

$$
{x}_{1}=-\frac{3}{10}+\frac{1}{3}{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{10}+\frac{1}{3}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{10} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3} \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
-10a+\frac{6b}{c}=-10\cdot (-\frac{3}{10})+\frac{6\cdot (\frac{1}{3})}{1}=5.
$$

$$

$$

content.problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}=2 \\ {x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=2 \\ 2{x}_{1}-8{x}_{2}=4\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear equations shown above. If the general least-squares solution of the system is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R
$$

what is the value of $3a+\frac{b}{c}?$
content.worked_solution:
First, we write our system in matrix form as $Ax=b,$ where 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 \\ 1 & -4 \\ 2 & -8\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

The least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

$$
{A}^{T}\,Ax={A}^{T}b
$$

Notice that the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent. So first, let's write down the normal equation in matrix form:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 2 \\ 4 & -4 & -8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 \\ 1 & -4 \\ 2 & -8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 2 \\ 4 & -4 & -8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}6 & -24 \\ -24 & 96\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -32\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the final matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}6 & -24 & 8 \\ -24 & 96 & -32\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}6 & -24 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we have 

$$
{x}_{1}=\frac{4}{3}+4{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{3}+4{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{3} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
3a+\frac{b}{c}=3\cdot \frac{4}{3}+\frac{4}{1}=8.
$$
